c.tagline: Thailand's northernmost major city, home to a dazzling white temple and gateway to the Golden Triangle

card: Accepted at larger hotels and restaurants; cash preferred at markets

taxi.fareNote: Songthaews and tuk-tuks are the standard way around town; Grab is available for longer trips

emergency.note: Tourist police (1155) can assist with English-language support

religion: Christianity and animist traditions (notable among hill tribe communities)
walk: Central Chiang Rai's temples and night bazaar are walkable; the White Temple, Blue Temple, and Golden Triangle require a car, songthaew, or tour

safety.safety: Very safe city, popular with independent travelers
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; standard travel caution applies near the Golden Triangle border area

hood_landmark.City Center / Night Bazaar: Chiang Rai's Night Bazaar and Clock Tower
hood_landmark.Wat Rong Khun (White Temple): Wat Rong Khun's dazzling white contemporary temple
hood_landmark.Wat Rong Suea Ten (Blue Temple): Wat Rong Suea Ten's vivid blue temple hall
hood_landmark.Golden Triangle: The Golden Triangle's Thailand-Laos-Myanmar river confluence
hood_landmark.Doi Mae Salong: Doi Mae Salong's hilltop tea plantations

hood_desc: The compact downtown with the night bazaar, clock tower, and most hotels and restaurants; the natural base for any visit.
A striking contemporary all-white temple complex on the edge of town, one of Thailand's most photographed modern landmarks.
A vividly blue temple a short drive from downtown, a newer but equally photogenic counterpart to the White Temple.
The historic river confluence where Thailand, Laos, and Myanmar meet, about an hour from the city.
A hilltop Yunnanese Chinese settlement amid tea plantations, offering cooler air and a distinct cultural feel.
lodging: Budget lodges near Wat Rong Khun
Anantara Golden Triangle Elephant Camp & Resort
Doi Mae Salong tea plantation guesthouses

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water instead of tap.

transit.sys: Songthaews and tuk-tuks around town; Grab for longer trips
transit.pay: Cash fare or Grab app payment
transit.map: Not centrally published; songthaews run informal routes
transit.note: Renting a scooter or car is common for reaching the temples and Golden Triangle independently

transport.air: Mae Fah Luang-Chiang Rai International Airport (CEI), about 15 min from downtown
transport.train: No passenger rail service to Chiang Rai
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Chiang Mai (about 3 hr) and Bangkok (about 11-12 hr)
transport.car: Rental cars and scooters available; well connected via Highway 1 to Chiang Mai

airport.name: Mae Fah Luang-Chiang Rai International Airport

net.m: Good 4G coverage in town, patchier in rural hill areas
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An AIS or DTAC tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory but appreciated for tour guides
